method.description: Identity resolution only. The revision asserted inside the assigned document ID was tested against the issuer's own published labelling as recorded in the acquisition intelligence, and the recorded automated-retrieval block was re-tested by HEAD request so no document body was transferred. No binary was acquired.
method.restrictedDocumentAcquiredNote: The Kansas Judicial Council forms are restricted to non-commercial use. This job deliberately did not retrieve the document body. The block re-test used HEAD only, which returns headers without transferring content, so nothing restricted was obtained merely because it might have been obtainable.

evidence: Three independent Kansas Judicial Council document pages all label the file 'Criminal Cover Sheet (12-2014)'.
No official Kansas source — Judicial Council, Supreme Court, Office of Judicial Administration, or any statewide index — publishes a Criminal Cover Sheet revised 10/14/2025.

The queue's own recorded title, 'Kansas Judicial Council / Kansas Judicial Branch Criminal Cover Sheet, revised 10/14/2025', carries the same uncorroborated date and is not independent evidence of it.

queueClaimAssessed.why: The document and its issuer are identified with confidence. The revision embedded in the document ID is not, and a confirmed-identity label that carries an unverified revision inside the identifier overstates what is known.

identityResolution.resolutionStatusNote: What is resolved is that 10/14/2025 is unsupported. Whether the correct identifier is the Council's 12-2014 revision is the likely answer but is not asserted here as fact: this job could not byte-verify the Council's file, because the publisher blocks automation and the document is commercially restricted.

options: Correct the document ID to the Council's published 12-2014 revision, or
Produce an official Kansas source for a 10/14/2025 revision.
requiredCorrection.doNotDoBoth: Do not retain the 2025 identifier while citing the 12-2014 file as its source. That is the current state and it is what makes the row unverifiable.
requiredCorrection.notAppliedRationale: Changing the expected document ID touches the legal-design track-source relationships and the source-acquisition queue, both forbidden paths for this job.

substitutionHazards.hazard: Substituting the Kansas Judicial Branch civil cover sheet
substitutionHazards.why: The Judicial Branch forms page publishes a civil cover sheet only and no criminal cover sheet. The civil form is a different document for different proceedings. Its availability, and the fact that it sits outside the Council's restriction, is not a reason to bind it to a criminal expungement component.
substitutionHazards.consequence: There is therefore no unrestricted statewide alternative to the Council's criminal cover sheet. Availability of a similarly named form is not identity.

substitutionHazards.why: The Council's forms are copyrighted and restricted to non-commercial use. Even were the 403 to lift, obtaining the file would not confer a right to use it in a commercial product. Identity and permission are separate gates.

substitutionHazards.hazard: Inferring statewide identity from a local district's cover sheet
substitutionHazards.why: Kansas Supreme Court Rule 123(a) requires substantial compliance with the forms on the judicial council website, which makes the Council's form the statewide reference. A district's own sheet is not a substitute identity for it.

automationBlockRetest.recordedStatus: BLOCKED — HTTP 403 to all automated agents including a full Chrome user-agent
automationBlockRetest.method: HEAD requests only, full Chrome user-agent, no body transfer
automationBlockRetest.conclusion: The Kansas block reproduces in full and is current. It is a publisher block, not absence — the documents are published and reachable by a human browser.
automationBlockRetest.contrastNote: This is the opposite result from the Colorado host tested in the same cycle, where the recorded 403 did not reproduce. The two must not be generalised to each other.

separateDefectRaised.observed: The component's legalBasis list includes K.S.A. 20-173.
separateDefectRaised.assessment: K.S.A. 20-173 is the specialty-court statute. It may well be authority for the specialty-court track, but it is not authority for a cover sheet. The cover-sheet requirement comes from Kansas Supreme Court Rule 123(a), which no cover-sheet row cites.
separateDefectRaised.recommendation: Remove K.S.A. 20-173 as a cover-sheet basis and cite Rule 123(a) instead. Raised as a separate defect; not corrected here.

ruleInterpretationReferral.question: Rule 123(a)(1) provides that the cover sheet is not retained in the case file. Does a document that is not retained in the case file need to be generated by the product at all, and does the Council's non-commercial restriction bite on a sheet that the court discards?
ruleInterpretationReferral.scopeWarning: This must be referred as a question about one ministerial court-administration document only. It must never be used as a template for the substantive Kansas Judicial Council forms — the petitions and orders — whose restriction is addressed separately under EXC-01.

commercialGate.note: Resolving the cover-sheet identity does not clear the Kansas Judicial Council commercial-use restriction. The edition disposition for this row is commercial_use_hold and it remains in force. The terminal commercial determination is made under EXC-01, not here.

unresolved.question: Where did '10/14/2025' come from?
unresolved.why: No official Kansas source publishes that revision, and this job found no provenance for it in the repository beyond the queue title that repeats it. It may be a capture date, a local district variant, or a transcription error. Recorded as unexplained rather than assumed to be an error of any particular kind.

unresolved.question: Is the Council's 12-2014 file byte-identical to anything the repository expects?
unresolved.why: The repository holds no binary for this row, the publisher blocks automated retrieval, and the document is commercially restricted so it was deliberately not fetched.
